headline: Highest risk is medium: AutoGPT can write files and use shell while Superset reads APIs, creating default-path prompt, data, and workflow coupling without direct evidence of a shared channel.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: AutoGPT can use the filesystem and shell, while Superset exposes an API surface; however, no shared channel or direct ingestion path is documented. The pairwise prompt-injection pathway is therefore possible only through unusual operator bridging, not by default.
conditions: IF the operator copies AutoGPT-generated text into Superset-managed content or prompts, injection becomes possible.
IF both agents are connected through a shared file or message channel, one agent can influence the other.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces.
Disable copy-paste of agent output into operational prompts.
Require manual review before any content is imported into Superset.
Use provenance labels on files exchanged between agents.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Neither profile shows touched sensitive data classes, and both are open-source with docs-only evidence. AutoGPT can access the filesystem and Superset can call its API, so leakage is plausible only if the operator places sensitive files in a shared location or routes them through either agent.
conditions: IF sensitive files are placed in a shared workspace, AutoGPT may read them.
IF Superset is configured to ingest those files or API payloads, the data can flow onward.
mitigations: Store sensitive data outside any shared directory.
Restrict API inputs to non-sensitive test data.
Review filesystem permissions before running both agents.
Turn on least-privilege access for any shared storage.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: AutoGPT has shell and filesystem write capability, while Superset exposes an API surface; overlapping mutable access can conflict if both operate on the same workspace or backend. No locking or coordination primitive is documented, so uncertainty pushes this to medium rather than low.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same directory or shared backend, concurrent edits can collide.
IF the operator runs multiple AutoGPT instances despite supports_multiple_instances=false, state conflicts become more likely.
mitigations: Assign separate directories to each agent.
Avoid concurrent writes to shared resources.
Check for stale locks before starting a run.

D_cascading_error.rationale: AutoGPT can generate outputs from shell/file activity, and Superset can consume API-driven inputs; if Superset treats AutoGPT output as authoritative, errors can cascade into dashboards or downstream actions. There is no documented verification step, so the interaction is plausible in default workflows.
conditions: IF Superset ingests AutoGPT-produced files or payloads without validation, incorrect facts can propagate.
IF the operator uses AutoGPT output as a source of truth for Superset content, downstream errors can spread.
mitigations: Add a human verification step before ingestion.
Validate schemas on all AutoGPT outputs.
Use read-only review mode for generated artifacts.
Reject untrusted fields in Superset import paths.

E_compliance.rationale: No data residency, certification, retention, or subject-rights mismatch is documented for either agent, and both profiles show no touched sensitive data classes. With only docs-level evidence, a compliance breach pathway is not established.
conditions: IF future deployment routes regulated data through either agent, compliance review is required.
IF residency or retention settings differ in the actual deployment, reassess the pair.
mitigations: Document the data classes before deployment.
Confirm retention settings for both systems.
Keep regulated data out of the pair until reviewed.
